findings: No acceptance target passes: every torque is 27-36% above the paper's. At 22 A and 56.5 degrees the model gives 20.66 N m for the proposed rotor against 15.63 (x1.322), 20.40 against 15.04 for method 1 (x1.357), 20.74 against 15.41 for method 2 (x1.346) and 18.47 against 14.50 for method 3 (x1.274). Torque from the flux linkages agrees with the band's within 0.05% in every build.

The excess is a nearly uniform scale. The prototype's torque against current angle at 2/3 of rated current is 1.277-1.297 times Fig. 11's simulated points at all eight angles, and normalized to their peaks the model's curve and the paper's agree within 1.1% (within 0.6% for Table 3's proposed rotor): the angle of maximum torque and the curve's shape, which saturation and the d/q inductance ratio set, are reproduced; the magnitude is not.

Because the factor is the same at rated and at 2/3 of rated current while saturation is reproduced, it does not behave like an error in the winding's ampere-turns (turns, parallel paths or current), which would change torque differently at the two currents. It behaves like an effective length: the paper's results correspond to about 106 mm of the 140 mm stack, which the paper does not state. Its rated 15.63 N m at 6000 rpm is 9.8 kW, consistent with the stated 10 kW; the model's 20.7 N m would be 13 kW. The cause is open.

Controls change the proposed rotor's torque by: mesh 0.7 times +0.05%; tooth tips 1.2 mm deep -0.2%; a 0.8 mm rib -2.4%; barrier ends as wide as the barriers -3.2%; M-45 steel -0.9%; a magnetic shaft 0.0%. 22 A read as the amplitude gives 12.06 N m (-23% against the paper) and distorts the torque-angle curve (9% shape deviation), so the rms reading is the one whose curve matches.

The ranking of Table 3 is reproduced except for one swap: method 3 lowest and method 1 below the proposed rotor, as in the paper, but method 2 comes out 0.4% above the proposed rotor where the paper has it 1.4% below.

Torque ripple (not a target) does not correspond: 48.4%, 15.6%, 60.8% and 34.2% for the proposed rotor and methods 1-3, against the paper's 12.63%, 36.3%, 23.38% and 42.34%; mesh refinement leaves 48.4%. Ripple depends on where the barrier ends sit against the stator slots, so the model's ends (angle reference, end width) evidently differ from the authors'.

At rated current the model's per-phase inductances are Ld 17.4 mH and Lq 1.9 mH; Fig. 10's simulated values at those currents are about 16 and 3.3 mH, but they include end-winding inductance, so they are not compared.

Fresh look (2026-10-27), with the authors' Energies 2017 paper on the same lamination (case ibrahim-2017-ferrite-pmasynrm; diagnostics outside both frozen cases, ~/code/femm-brain-work/papers/synrm/fresh/diag.py, summary.json). That paper's Fig. 3a is drawn to scale: its stator is this case's Fig. A1 within 0.05 mm (5.14 mm teeth, 2.80 mm openings, a 101.1 mm2 slot against the stated 100 mm2), at the same 140 mm, 0.3 mm gap and 36/4 slots and poles. The brain's construction does not reproduce that paper's Maxwell torque at 140 mm exactly either, but its excess there is smaller and of another kind: +16.7% at half, +10.4% at 10.59 A and +7.5% at rated current, the optimal current angles matched, larger where the gap dominates. A 0.06 mm longer effective gap (0.36 mm) removes it: within -1.3 to +0.5% at the three currents, Fig. 5's torque against current angle within -0.9 to +3.2% at seven further angles and +5.8% at the eighth, its smallest torque (2.4 N m; at 0.30 mm: +4.7 to +25.5%), and the unfitted star-delta data tip within +0.5%.

This case's results are not that paper's model: with the 0.36 mm gap its targets still exceed, by 1.228 for Table 3's proposed rotor and 1.09-1.21 across Fig. 11, now tilted with current angle, whereas at the stated 0.30 mm gap Fig. 11 is a flat 1.28-1.30 (and the proposed rotor 1.32). This paper's own FE inductances say the same: Fig. 10's Ld (with end winding) is 0.93-0.95 of the 0.30 mm build's at every current from 1.5 to 26.5 A (peak reading, knee aligned), but 0.97-1.11 of the 0.36 mm build's. So the 2016 FE behaves like this case's construction at the stated gap scaled uniformly by about 0.77 (as an unstated effective length of 106-109 mm, or a flux scale, would make it), while the 2017 FE of the same authors behaves like it at a 0.36 mm gap without a scale. The 30% lies in this paper; its FE and its measurements (Fig. 11) agree with each other, so the prototype as tested may differ from the stated one, or the FE was scaled; the paper gives nothing to tell which. Cause localized, not identified.

This case's readings stand. The paper's FE plot (Fig. 3a, the reference design) overlaps the prototype as built here with IoU 0.85 (91% of its low-field barrier pixels inside), against 0.58 for the 2017 rotor; building this case with the 2017 drawing's stator (tapered shoes, measured slot) changes the rated torque +0.2% (20.69 N m); the 2017 rotor in this case's conditions gives 19.96 N m, and this case's proposed rotor in the 2017 machine 19.62 against the drawn rotor's 18.81, so the rotors differ by about 4%, not 30%. FEMM's lower Metals Handbook M-43/M-36 curve lowers the rated torque 4.7% (19.69) and Fig. 11 by 2-5%, distorting its shape (ratios 1.21-1.27).

The stated parameters are consistent with the 2017 machine; the two are different machines on one stator lamination. 15 turns per slot at 22/2 A carry 165 A per slot (rms) against 26 turns at 12.23/2 A, 159 A; in the 2017 slot's copper (26 x 1.573 mm2) that is 4.03 against 3.89 A/mm2; 90 series turns per path at 200 Hz against 156 at 100 Hz need 15% more voltage at equal flux. Each rating is its own FE torque times its speed (15.63 N m x 6000 rpm = 9.8 kW; 17.50 N m x 3000 rpm = 5.50 kW), so the ratings confirm nothing independently. The 2016 prototype has the Table A1 rotor and M400-50A, the 2017 prototypes an optimized rotor and M270/M330-50A. The brain's rated flux linkage gives 465 V (line) at 6000 rpm for this machine, 393 V at 3000 rpm for the 2017 one (380 V rated); a 0.77 flux scale would bring this one to 358 V. No measurement procedure here was wrong: the frozen inputs, targets and record stand.
retrospective: Longest: the rotor. Fig. 2 defines the barriers only by labelled arrows (p_b, L_b, W_b, theta_b), the rib is never given and the 'end arc' is described two ways; the authors' FE plot (Fig. 3a) settled the barrier shape but not its dimensions.

The skill lacked a step for checking a paper's operating point against its own rating before freezing (15.63 N m at 6000 rpm is the stated 10 kW, so the magnitudes are self-consistent) and for comparing curve shapes as well as values: a uniform factor across operating points with the right shape points at a scale (length, convention) rather than at geometry or materials. Both are lessons now.
Lessons that held: read geometry from the authors' FE rendering; give every assumption a control (here none of them moves the torque by more than 3.2%, which is itself the finding).
Added generically: flux_barrier_rotor (barriers symmetric about each q-axis with tapering legs, rounded ends and tangential ribs) for synchronous reluctance and PM-assisted rotors.

Fresh look (2026-10-27). Longest: separating the two papers' discrepancies, which needed the second paper replicated in full and about 1,000 diagnostic solves; the decisive tests were cheap once the right quantities were chosen: the ratio's dependence on current (a gap's signature in 2017) and on current angle (a flat ratio, a scale, here).

What the skill lacked: a step for using another paper on the same hardware as a transfer standard. A uniform factor that no control moves is either the construction or the paper; replicating the authors' sibling paper with the same construction separates the two (here: a gap-like 7.5-16.7% in the 2017 paper's model, which this paper's results do not show, and a uniform 0.77 in this paper alone). Proposed for SKILL.md (section 8 or the gap step): when a case fails by a scale, search the authors' other papers for the same lamination or prototype and replicate one before recording the cause as open; compare both the ratio's current dependence and its current-angle dependence.

Lessons that held: compare shapes as well as values (it separated the two papers here); a fitted gap-steel pair from a small grid (Hamouda) found the 2017 discrepancy, confirmed on results not fitted. A lesson corrected: a rating is no independent check when it is the FE torque times the speed (both papers' ratings are).
Generic additions from the sibling case: slot_winding, library_material overrides and the dq_linkage maximum over current angles (ibrahim-2017-ferrite-pmasynrm).
